resources.string: How insulin helps cells take up glucose
Outside the cell, insulin binds a receptor on the cell membrane.
Inside the cell, the activated receptor phosphorylates an insulin receptor substrate (IRS).
PI3K and AKT relay the signal
IRS helps recruit PI3K. PI3K changes the membrane lipid PIP2 into PIP3, which helps recruit and activate AKT.
A GLUT4 vesicle fuses with the membrane
The signal promotes fusion of GLUT4-containing vesicles with the cell membrane, increasing the amount of GLUT4 at the surface.
GLUT4 facilitates glucose entry down its concentration gradient. Insulin stays outside the cell in this illustration.
Simplified skeletal muscle and fat cell pathway. Shapes, distances and playback time are not to scale; this is not a blood glucose prediction.
